_note: Carriers other than seagoing hulls and animals (those are in 99_ships.json and 90_additions.json): the vehicles and rigs that carriage wears out (Complaints/629). Every mass, hour count and allocation is an estimate marked in each yield_basis. carrier_use.serves names which geography mode carrier input the good supplies; days_per_year is the days a unit works in a year.

cart.basis: per two-wheeled cart without its team or harness
cart.yield_basis: MASS: geography's CART_SELF_MASS_KG (sim/geography/transport.py), 200 kg empty, cited there as 150-250 kg for a two-wheeled wood-and-iron cart; allocated here as 0.25 m3 of retained timber at the timber recipe density of 600 kg/m3 (150 kg) plus about 15 kg of iron tyre strips, nails and axle fittings; 0.4 m3 is bought to allow shaping offcuts. LABOUR: 150 carpenter hours (wheel making is most of it) and 15 smith hours are TEMPORARY HEURISTICS, confidence D, no source found, not a measured work log. No price sets the bill. Retire when a measured wheelwright's work log is found (complaint 629 follow-up). NAILS: 3 of the 15 kg of iron are nails and small fittings (nails_kg) and 12 kg is bar, the split is a LABELLED HEURISTIC, conf D, no source found; retire: Complaints/533.

pack_saddle.basis: per wood-framed pack saddle with girth and breeching rigging, for one animal
pack_saddle.yield_basis: MASS: geography's PACK_SADDLE_MASS_KG, 15 kg for a loaded rig before cargo (10-20 kg cited there). Allocated as a wooden frame of about 0.01 m3 (6 kg at 600 kg/m3; 0.02 m3 bought), 6 kg of leather and 2 kg of cord for girths and padding. LABOUR: 40 leatherworker (saddler) and 10 carpenter hours are TEMPORARY HEURISTICS, confidence D, author's estimates. Retire with a measured saddler's work log (complaint 629 follow-up).

river_barge.basis: per flat-bottomed river or canal barge towed from a path, without cargo or team
river_barge.yield_basis: MASS: geography's BARGE_SELF_MASS_KG (sim/geography/transport.py), 3000 kg empty (a few tonnes, confidence D there). Allocated as 4.5 m3 of retained timber at 600 kg/m3 (about 2700 kg) plus 30 kg iron fastenings, 40 kg tar and 20 kg cord; 5 m3 is bought for offcuts. LABOUR: about a sixth of the merchant ship's shipwright hours, with a helper share like the ship's; TEMPORARY HEURISTICS, confidence D. Retire with measured barge scantlings and build logs (complaint 629 follow-up).
